newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian sentenced to death for swindling investors.
newsitem.headline: Iranian sentenced to death for swindling investors.

text.p: An Iranian businessman was sentenced to death for swindling thousands of investors, corruption and embezzlement, Iran's official news agency IRNA said on Thursday.

"Hoseyn Dowlatkhah was found guilty of embezzlement and corruption on Wednesday and sentenced to death. He was accused of taking the money of some 7,000 depositors," said IRNA, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Dowlatkhah launched an appeal which would be referred to the supreme court, the agency said.
The court also confiscated his property and cash and used it to repay most of the debts he owed, it said. Debts to depositors were estimated at nearly 90 billion rials ($30 million).

His firm began collecting money in 1983 and was banned seven years later after 7,000 depositers lodged complaints against it, IRNA said. Some of the money had been transferred abroad. Investigations into the firm's dealings lasted five years.
